P.h: 16-year-old UEFI flaw lets attackers run ring 0 code before Secure Boot loads
P.p: A buffer overflow in TianoCore EDK2's PXE Base Code driver, scored CVSS 9.5, sits in the reference UEFI code behind most server firmware. An oversized ICMP error during network boot allowed code execution in ring 0, before Secure Boot and the TPM chain of trust loaded.
P.s: An AMI pull request leaked the fix months before a January coordinated disclosure. Exploitation needs local network access and per-model address tuning. Request patched firmware from your vendors, disable PXE boot where feasible, and watch network boot segments for odd ICMP traffic.

items.h: Sony ISP unit breach exposes 2.5M So-net records

items.h: Skyw4lker device-code phishing targets US firms
items.d: Password-protected contract lures route victims through Google Sites into real Microsoft sign-in flows. Completing the attacker-started authorization hands over Microsoft 365 tokens.

items.h: AI 'hacker' finds 4 severe EPICS bugs in under 4 hours
items.d: Causal Security's Cipher found one critical integer overflow rated CVSS 9.8 that could enable remote code execution, plus three high-severity flaws. EPICS controls particle accelerators and fusion experiments.

items.h: AI now runs real attacks against Japan
items.d: TrendAI documents CyberStrikeAI coordinating 44 agents against at least 19 organizations. Victim-side confirmation remains incomplete.

P.h: Anthropic model builds exploit chains in browsers, mobile OSes and kernels
P.p: Anthropic researchers used an internal research model to find critical vulnerabilities and construct multi-step exploit chains in widely used software, including remote code execution, sandbox escapes and lock-screen bypasses. All were reported to vendors under coordinated disclosure.
P.s: Anthropic argues AI-assisted discovery can help defenders patch before attackers strike. TLDR also reports Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, strong in cybersecurity, is limited to selected defenders until guardrails improve.

P.h: GitHub swaps repo-wide write locks for per-reference quorums
P.p: To overcome cross-region latency during its Azure migration, GitHub is replacing repository-wide write serialization with per-reference quorums. Internal tests showed 3 to 4 times higher throughput for writes to different references.
P.s: An object-storage-backed design also lets read capacity scale independently. Separately, vLLM 0.31 reaches 100% tool-call schema accuracy for Kimi and DeepSeek through constrained decoding, fixing an 8% invalid-call rate in 0.28.
